about: Phase 8's hand labels (owner, 14 Nov 2026: option B): every entry point in Rallly and Documenso (packages/ee aside, which is never enabled), a fixed set of modules in LibreChat and Twenty covering each framework they use, and the event props in 5 chosen screens per fork. Built without the detectors: each fork's files read with text scans and hand-written readers of its routers (tRPC objects, Express mounts, <Route> trees, NestJS decorators), and every difference with the engine read in the code and settled, at the pins below. Each entry is where the engine places it: a route at its registering call or object, a file's page at its default export, a decorated method at its name, a script at its key. 'convention' and 'code' are the bar's groups (100% recall for convention; at least 95% per fork for code; 100% precision).

notes: The OAuth integration's three routes are made by a factory whose base path is its argument ('/api/integrations' at its one call): labelled with their real paths; the engine lists them under /:unknown, not fully detected.

Route handlers handing every request to a Hono app (handle(app), directly or through OAuthIntegration's returned handler) aren't entry points; the v1 API's handler rewrites the path and is one (decisions log, 14 Nov 2026).
The app's base path is NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH's value, written {NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH} (owner, 14 Nov 2026).
packages/ee isn't labelled. ts-rest's v1 routes and the jobs board are mounted at run time: they aren't Hono routes.

Express modules: auth, oauth, convos, messages, agents/ and files/ (files' router is made by initialize() when the server starts; its sub-routers include agents' avatar router). React Router: client/src/routes (its /d/* routes redirect, so aren't screens).

NestJS: the auth controllers, the core REST controller and the API-key controller (both of its paths); GraphQL: the auth and workspace resolvers; React Router: SettingsRoutes.tsx, mounted at /settings (its legacy paths redirect); Next.js: the website.
